'''Jabari Montsho Smith Jr.''' (born May 13, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]].

Born in [[Fayetteville, Georgia]], to former professional basketball player [[Jabari Smith|Jabari Smith Sr.]], Smith began playing basketball at a young age under his father's mentorship. Smith attended [[Sandy Creek High School]], where in his senior year the team made a state championship appearance. In high school, Smith was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] and [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]]. A five star prospect ranked the nation's number seven overall recruit, he committed to [[Auburn University]] to play [[college basketball]]. As a freshman at Auburn, Smith helped the team achieve their first ever [[AP Poll|AP poll]] number one ranking and an [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) regular season championship. At the conclusion of his freshman year, Smith was named an [[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]], and won the [[USBWA National Freshman of the Year|USBWA National Freshman of the Year Award]]. Following his freshman season, Smith would declare for the [[2022 NBA draft]] and was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the third overall pick. He is also a distant cousin of NBA player [[Kwame Brown]].

==Early life==
Smith was born on May 13, 2003, in [[Fayetteville, Georgia]], to [[Jabari Smith |Jabari Smith Sr.]] and Taneskia Purnell. His father played [[college basketball]] at [[Louisiana State University|LSU]], and had a four-year career in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]], before playing overseas in Spain, Turkey, Iran and Puerto Rico.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |last1=Fader |first1=Mirin |title=The Drive Behind Jabari Smith Jr.|url=https://www.theringer.com/2022/2/4/22916297/jabari-smith-jr-auburn-nba-draft|website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|date=February 4, 2022}}</ref> Smith began playing [[basketball]] when he was five, and was trained by his father.<ref name=":2" /> His father while in the NBA had noticed the arrival of tall [[List of NBA players born outside the United States|international players]] with strong shooting, and decided to mold Smith as a player that despite his tall height, would win with shooting rather than with size.<ref name=":3">{{cite web |last1=Woo |first1=Jeremy |title=With His Mesmerizing Jumper, Jabari Smith Is the Fulcrum of Auburn's Ascent |url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/02/23/jabari-smith-auburn-basketball-nba-daily-cover |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=February 23, 2022}}</ref> At the age of 15, Smith would join the Atlanta Celtics on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit, coached by the father of star Auburn point guard [[Jared Harper]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name="bennett">{{cite web |last1=Bennett |first1=Brian |title=Recruiting notebook: Jabari Smith Jr. first setting his sights on a state title |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2088102/2020/09/25/jabari-smith-jr-recruiting-alabama-tennessee-georgia-auburn-lsu/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=October 10, 2020 |date=September 25, 2020}}</ref>

Smith started playing [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball as a sophomore at [[Sandy Creek High School]] in [[Tyrone, Georgia]].<ref name="krohn">{{cite web |last1=Krohn |first1=Adam |title=Sandy Creek's Smith making name for himself |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/sandy-creek-smith-making-name-for-himself/P1Fdw7ySCvoCPB2dYfOBdM/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=October 10, 2020 |date=January 23, 2019}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 24.5 points, 10.8 rebounds, and 2.8 blocks per game.<ref name="vitale">{{cite web |last1=Vitale |first1=Josh |title=5-star 2021 PF Jabari Smith becomes highest-rated commitment in Auburn basketball history |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2020/10/09/auburn-basketball-recruiting-2021-power-forward-jabari-smith-five-star-commitment-bruce-pearl/5937593002/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=October 10, 2020 |date=October 9, 2020}}</ref> In his senior season, Smith averaged 24 points, 10 rebounds, three steals, and three blocks per game, leading his team to a Class 3A state runner-up finish. He was named [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]], Georgia [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and ''[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]'' All-Classification Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Holcomb |first1=Todd |title=Boys basketball player of year: Jabari Smith |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/high-school-sports-blog/boys-basketball-player-of-year-jabari-smith-ii/RHYDVPOD6BDRDAYVHOHK2HWYU4/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=April 2, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Stultz |first1=Brian |title=Jabari Smith Jr. named Georgia's Gatorade Player of the Year |url=https://auburnwire.usatoday.com/2021/06/04/jabari-smith-jr-named-georgias-gatorade-player-of-the-year/ |website=Auburn Wire |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=June 4, 2021 |archive-date=June 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210621042652/https://auburnwire.usatoday.com/2021/06/04/jabari-smith-jr-named-georgias-gatorade-player-of-the-year/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sandy Creek's Smith named Mr. Georgia Basketball |url=https://thecitizen.com/2021/03/29/sandy-creeks-smith-named-mr-georgia-basketball/ |website=The Citizen |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=March 29, 2021}}</ref> Smith was selected to the rosters for the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] and finished as a runner up for [[Mr. Basketball USA]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Green |first1=Tom |title=Auburn signee Jabari Smith makes McDonald's All-America team |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2021/02/auburn-signee-jabari-smith-makes-mcdonalds-all-america-team.html |website=[[The Birmingham News]] |access-date=October 3, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Jabari Smith Jr.jpg|thumb|upright|Smith with the Auburn Tigers in 2022]]
Smith was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 Top Basketball Recruits |url=https://247sports.com/Season/2021-Basketball/CompositeRecruitRankings/?InstitutionGroup=HighSchool |access-date=October 25, 2022 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ESPN Basketball Recruiting - Player Rankings |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings |access-date=October 25, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jabari Smith, 2021 Power Forward - Rivals.com |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/jabari-smith-236999 |access-date=October 25, 2022 |website=n.rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> On October 9, 2020, he announced his commitment to play college basketball for [[Auburn University]] over offers from [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]], [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. Upon his commitment he became the highest ranked player to commit to Auburn in the modern recruiting era.<ref name=":4">{{cite web |last1=Biancardi |first1=Paul |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |title=Top-five senior Jabari Smith commits to Auburn Tigers |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30080021/top-five-senior-jabari-smith-commits-auburn-tigers-coach-bruce-pearl |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=October 10, 2020 |date=October 9, 2020}}</ref> Smith has said that he committed to Auburn due to his fit within the teams play style under head coach [[Bruce Pearl]], the school's relatively close proximity to his hometown and because the school could provide him a more traditional college experience than he would get elsewhere.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4" />

== Professional career ==

=== Houston Rockets (2022–present) ===

==== 2022–23 season: Rookie season ====
Prior to the [[2022 NBA draft]], Smith was believed by many analysts and insiders to be the number one overall pick, with Smith even saying that he would be surprised not to be picked number one by the [[Orlando Magic]] with [[ESPN]]'s [[Adrian Wojnarowski]] on the morning off the draft on Orlando plan's to finalize selecting Smith first overall .<ref>{{Cite web |last=Purdum |first=David |date=June 22, 2022 |title=Auburn Tigers' Jabari Smith favored to be No. 1 pick in heavily bet NBA draft|website=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/sports-betting/story/_/id/34131494/auburn-tigers-jabari-smith-favored-no-1-pick-heavily-bet-nba-draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=June 23, 2022 |title=Report: Jabari Smith Jr. expected to be drafted first by Magic|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/06/23/magic-nba-draft-jabari-smith-chet-holmgren/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayne Sports|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/2022-nba-draft-jabari-smith-says-ill-be-surprised-if-im-not-taken-no-1-by-the-orlando-magic-144429878.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=x.com |url=https://x.com/wojespn/status/1539951821405429761?lang=en |access-date=2024-05-27 |website=X (formerly Twitter)}}</ref> However the Magic ended up selecting [[Paolo Banchero]] and Smith ending up being selected with third overall pick by the [[Houston Rockets]], making him the highest drafted player to ever come out of Auburn, surpassing [[Chris Morris (basketball)|Chris Morris]] and [[Chuck |access-date=June 23, 2022}}</ref> The [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] promised if he was available Smith would be selected 2nd overall but they instead selected [[Chet Holmgren]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-15 |title=Report: Jabari Smith Jr. wanted to be drafted by the Thunder |url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2023/02/15/report-jabari-smith-jr-wanted-to-be-drafted-by-the-thunder/ He made his [[2022 NBA Summer League|summer league debut]] with 10 points, seven rebounds, three assists, and a steal in a 91–77 loss against the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston vs. Orlando - Box Score - July 7, 2022 - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba-summer/boxscore/_/gameId/401451017 |access-date=July 8, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On October 2, 2022, Smith made his preseason debut, scoring 21 points with 5-of-8 shooting from three along with eight rebounds and two assists in a 134–96 win against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shapiro |first=Michael |date=October 2, 2022 |title=Houston's Jabari Smith flashes smooth shooting stroke in preseason debut |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/jabari-smith-impresses-preseason-debut-17482282.php |access-date=October 2, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Coty |date=October 2, 2022 |title=Jabari Smith Jr. Shines in Rockets Preseason Win Over Spurs |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/.amp/news/jabari-smith-jr-houston-rockets-preseason-win-over-spurs-jalen-green |access-date=October 2, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Doric |first=Sam |date=October 3, 2022 |title=Jabari Smith Jr. 'Exactly As Advertised' in Rockets' Preseason Win Over Spurs |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10051014-jabari-smith-jr-exactly-as-advertised-in-rockets-preseason-win-over-spurs |access-date=October 3, 2022}}</ref> On October 19, Smith made his regular season debut, scoring 17 points along with seven rebounds and an assist in a 117–107 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rockets vs. Hawks - He finished by shooting 7-of-12 from the field, including 3-of-5 from three-point range. The outing was the sixth straight game in which Smith made at least three 3-pointers, the second-longest streak in history by a rookie.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=December 2, 2022 |title=Rockets' Jabari Smith Jr. finding groove from 3-point range |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/12/03/rockets-jabari-smith-jr-3-point-range-stats/ |access-date=December 4, 2022 |website=The Rookie Wire |language=en-US}}</ref> On December 23, he recorded his sixth double-double with 24 points by shooting 58.8% from the field and 3-of-8 from three with 10 rebounds in a loss against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |date=December 23, 2022 |title=Takeaways: Jabari Smith Jr.'s career night not quite enough as Luka Doncic drops 50 for Mavs |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/takeaways-jabari-smith-jr-career-040743119.html}}</ref>

On January 13, 2023, Smith scored a then career-high 27 points with three blocks and eight rebounds in a game loss against the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2022 |title=Game Recap: Kings 139, Rockets 114 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/game-recap-kings-139-rockets-070059175.html |access-date=January 14, 2023 |website=sports.yahoo.com |language=en-US}}</ref> During a game against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on January 16, a mic’d up Smith informed [[LeBron James]] that “You played against [[Jabari Smith|my dad]], your first NBA game ever... Sacramento.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cwik |first=Chris |date=January 17, 2023|title=LeBron James reminded he's really old by Rockets rookie Jabari Smith Jr.: 'You played against my dad'|url= https://sports.yahoo.com/le-bron-james-reminded-hes-really-old-by-rockets-rookie-jabari-smith-jr-you-played-against-my-dad-164702888.html|access-date=April 5, 2025}}</ref> On March 9, Smith grabbed 12 rebounds and set a then career-high 30 points in a 134–125 overtime loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=M. Davis |first=Coty |date=March 10, 2023 |title=Rockets' Jabari Smith Jr. Records First 30-Point Game In Loss To Pacers: 'My Confidence Coming Back' |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/.amp/news/houston-rockets-jabari-smith-jr-30-point-game-loss-to-pacers-stephen-silas-jalen-green |access-date=March 10, 2023}}</ref> On March 14, Smith scored 24 points by shooting 83.8 percent from the field with 5 threes made and 11 rebounds in a game win against the [[Boston Celtics]]. In doing so, he became the first player in Rockets franchise to average 20-plus points and 10-plus rebounds in three straight games since [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] in 1985.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pagaduan |first=Jedd |date=March 14, 2023 |title=Jabari Smith Jr. tallies impressive Rockets rookie feat not seen since Hakeem Olajuwon |url=https://clutchpoints.com/rockets-news-jabari-smith-jr-tallies-impressive-houston-rookie-feat-not-seen-since-hakeem-olajuwon |access-date=March 14, 2023}}</ref> On March 17, Smith made a game-winning three-pointer in a 114–112 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/rockets-news-houston-fans-go-nuts-after-jabari-smith-jr-stuns-pelicans-at-the-buzzer|title='Jabari for the win!': Rockets fans going nuts after Jabari Smith Jr. stuns Pelicans at the buzzer|website=ClutchPoints|date=March 17, 2023|access-date=March 17, 2023}}</ref> At the conclusion of his rookie season he was voted to the All-Rookie second team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022-23 KIA NBA All-Rookie Second Team: Jabari Smith Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/nba-all-rookie-second-team-jabari-smith-jr?plsrc=nba&collection=2022-23-all-rookie-team |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=www.nba.com}}</ref>

==== 2023–24 season ====
On December 11, 2023, Smith scored a career high 34 points along with 13 rebounds in a 134–127 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shapiro |first=Michael |date=2023-12-21 |title=Jabari Smith Jr. torches hometown team in career-best night |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/jabari-smith-rockets-hawks-highlights-18567150.php |access-date=2023-12-24 |website=Chron |language=en}}</ref> On March 24, 2024, Smith was suspended one game after being involved in an altercation with [[Utah Jazz]] guard [[Kris Dunn]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marks |first=Bobby |date=March 24, 2024 |title=NBA suspends Kris Dunn two games, Jabari Smith Jr. one |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39802724/nba-suspends-kris-dunn-two-games-jabari-smith-jr-one |access-date=April 6, 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2024–25 season ====
On January 3, 2025, Smith suffered a fractured hand during Houston's practice prior to their game against the [[2024–25 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]]. He was subsequently ruled out for four-to-six weeks.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rockets F Jabari Smith Jr. out 4-6 weeks after breaking hand at shootaround|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/rockets-f-jabari-smith-jr-out-4-6-weeks-after-breaking-hand-at-shootaround-234949489.html|access-date=January 4, 2025|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref> Smith made 57 appearances (39 starts) for Houston during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 12.2 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 1.1 assists.

==== 2025–26 season ====
On June 30, 2025, Smith and the Rockets agreed to a five-year, $122 million contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2025 |title=Reports: Jabari Smith Jr., Rockets agree to 5-year, $122 million extensiin |url=https://www.nba.com/news/jabari-smith-jr-rockets-contract-extension |access-date=December 12, 2025 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Standing at 6 feet and 11 inches (2.11 meters) with a 7'1" feet (2.16 meters) wingspan and weighing 220 pounds (100 kilograms), Smith predominately plays the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position. Smith's length makes him a versatile player on both offense and defense. He often utilizes [[Jab step|jab-steps]] to help create space for his [[Jump shot (basketball)|jump shot]] and has range out to the [[Three-point field goal|three-point line]], shooting 42% from three-point range in college. On defense, he is mobile on the perimeter and physical inside, making him a candidate to defend big men but also switch comfortably onto [[Guard (basketball)|guards]]. Smith was noted for his defensive instincts and quick hands, averaging a [[Block (basketball)|block]] and a [[Steal (basketball)|steal]] per game in college. Many sources and scouts have compared his play making style to other big men such as [[Rashard Lewis]], [[Chris Bosh]], [[Michael Porter Jr.]] and [[Kevin Durant]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Irving |first=Kyle |date=June 23, 2022 |title=Jabari Smith Jr. NBA player comparisons |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/jabari-smith-jr-scouting-report-nba-draft-prospects-2022/otlbpxoyd7mz0ty2motpsdpq}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wasserman |first=Jonathan |date=June 13, 2022 |title=Pro Comparisons for Top Projected 2022 NBA Draft Picks |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2956722-pro-comparisons-for-top-projected-2022-nba-draft-picks |access-date=June 13, 2022}}</ref>

Scouts noted that Smith's main weakness on offense entering the draft is his ball handling, as he oftentimes struggles to generate offense off of the dribble.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Goldstone |first=Aaron |date=June 8, 2022 |title=Jabari smith jr mock draft |url=https://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2022/6/8/23148525/2022-nba-draft-jabari-smith-jr-scouting-report}}</ref>

==National team career==
Smith played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in [[Belém]], Brazil. He averaged 13.8 points and 6.2 rebounds per game and helped the United States win the gold medal.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Elite Forward Jabari Smith Jr. Has All the Tools |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jabari-smith-highlights-2021-sandy-creek-forwardhttps://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jabari-smith-highlights-2021-sandy-creek-forward |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=October 10, 2020 |date=March 24, 2020}}</ref>
